name: Belgium
summary: Black, yellow and red vertical bands in an unusual nearly square 13:15 ratio. The colours come from the arms of the Duchy of Brabant, and the vertical layout follows the French tricolour.
origin: Black, yellow and red were the colours of the Duchy of Brabant, whose arms are a golden lion with red claws and tongue on black. They were used in the Brabant Revolution of 1789 against Austrian rule.

During the Belgian Revolution of 1830 against the United Kingdom of the Netherlands, rebels at first used horizontal stripes. The Provisional Government adopted a vertical tricolour on 23 January 1831, following the French model, and the 1831 Constitution names the colours.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The black field of the Brabant arms.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The lion's red claws and tongue.

facts: The 13:15 ratio is used at the Belgian Parliament; most flags in practice are made in 2:3.
Germany uses the same three colours in horizontal bands, in a different order.
clues: Black, yellow and red vertical bands, almost square.
Its colours come from a golden lion with red claws on a black shield.
First flown with horizontal stripes during an 1830 revolution.
A larger neighbour uses the same colours horizontally.
